title: Random Color Generator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Random Color Generator: Generate random HEX and RGB colour values. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Random Color Generator](/random-color-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Generate random HEX and RGB colour values. Enter your number of colours and seed (deterministic — for games/demos only) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Generate random HEX and RGB colour values. This free online random color generator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Random Color Generator

Start by entering your number of colours, then entering your seed (deterministic — for games/demos only). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your number of colours.
2. Enter your seed (deterministic — for games/demos only).
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Red, green and blue channels are each selected from 0 to 255.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Random Color Generator](/random-color-generator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. RGB(255, 255, 255) is white and RGB(0, 0, 0) is black. ## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the units and labels before comparing results.
- Your entries stay in your browser and are not saved.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up or installation required. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Random Color Generator](/random-color-generator) and start straight away.

### Are my entries stored?

No. Calculations run in your browser and the tool does not save your entries. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What formula does the Random Color Generator use?

Red, green and blue channels are each selected from 0 to 255. You can see it in action in the [Random Color Generator](/random-color-generator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Random Color Generator?

Just Number of colours and Seed (deterministic — for games/demos only). Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
